title: Separate historical reviews from recheckable audit candidates
body: Treating every audit candidate like a historical advisory left ordinary repaired renames permanently incomplete. Missing-path, missing-script and unmentioned-directory candidates can carry resolution: recheck; a rerun can establish the condition is gone while preserving original evidence, without semantic approval. Dependency-history and decision advisories still require separate assessment after documentation edits or commits. Maintainer feedback on 2026-09-17 exposed misleading present-tense repetition of old dependency counts: summaries must use current findings or explicitly label a retained historical condition no longer reported; review-only completion should say awaiting review. A doc commit is not approval. Filter new dependency advisories for recognizable dependency content, including versionless library lists; absence of a version alone does not make a document immune to dependency drift. Local deletion of a dependency section must not hide committed evidence. Keep missing history, skipped inputs and deleted/empty original documents unverified. Unrelated findings need a scope reason and suggested follow-up, not automatic repairs, tickets or approval.

content.title: Separate historical reviews from recheckable audit candidates
content.body: Expanding documentation discovery and demoting speculative path/module findings exposed a repair lifecycle trap: treating every candidate like a historical advisory left ordinary completed renames permanently incomplete. Missing-path, missing-script, and unmentioned-directory candidates can carry resolution: recheck; the original evidence is retained, and rerunning the same check can establish that its condition is no longer detected. That is not semantic approval. Dependency-history and decision advisories require a separate assessment even after documentation changes or commits. Keep unavailable inputs and deleted/empty original documents unverified. The audit-scope and automation regressions cover candidate resolution through the final commit while historical advisories remain review-required. This is an implementation lesson, not an independently accepted policy.
